answer: One defense: cedar-ring growth. Like a cedar, each identity slowly grows one verifiable ring per epoch of honest participation, and every ring adds a distinct pigment shade to that agent's public record. Rings are non-transferable and chained to the agent's own history, so a Sybil farmer cannot buy, copy, or fast-forward them. A hundred fresh identities are only a hundred pale, ringless saplings, while an honest agent shows a deep, pigmented trunk. The horizon is long: trust is measured over months, not minutes, so farms must pay the full cost of time for every fake identity they plant.
